atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 建立字偶距规则
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 在字偶距页面为指定字符对新建一条规则并设定数值保存后，规则列表中出现对应该字符对的规则并显示字符对与设定数值。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 字偶距值作用于样文预览
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 为某字符对设定明显负值的字偶距（如 -100/1000 UPM）并保存后，样文预览中该字符对的间距相较设规则前明显收紧，其他字符对间距不变。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 混排样文碰撞定位到具体字符对
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 在包含多段中西文混排且存在至少一处重叠的样文中运行碰撞检测后，结果列出发生碰撞的具体字符对及其所在段落/位置（列表定位或样文中高亮标注均可），而非仅提示「存在碰撞」。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 重新校准、替换字形、修改指标均生成新版本
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 分别执行重新校准某页样张、替换某个已有字形、修改 UPM 或行距三类操作，每次操作后版本历史条目数加 1，并新增标注对应变更类型与时间戳的版本记录。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 历史版本不可覆盖
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 在存在版本 v1 的情况下修改字形或指标生成 v2 后，v1 仍存在于版本列表中且内容与编号保持不变，界面不提供覆盖或删除历史版本的操作。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 版本差异展示字形、指标与检查结果变化
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 对比相邻两个版本时，差异视图分别列出发生变化的字形（字符/格位标识及变更前后形态）、变化的指标项前后取值（如行距 1200→1400）以及检查结果的变化（问题条目的新增/消除或数量变化）。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 恢复旧版生成新版本
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 在存在 v1、v2、v3 的情况下对 v1 执行「恢复」后，版本列表新增一条新版本（条目数加 1）并标注其内容来源于 v1，v2 与 v3 仍保留，当前工作内容与 v1 一致。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 导出前执行完整性检查
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 在导出页面点击「导出」后，系统先执行完整性检查并展示检查结果摘要（通过项与问题项），检查完成前不直接产出字体文件。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 无效映射阻断构建
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 在保留一个重复映射或未指派 Unicode 的无效映射条目的情况下点击导出，构建被阻断、不生成 OTF 文件，并提示存在无效映射及其具体条目。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 轮廓错误阻断构建
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 在保留一个轮廓自交或开放路径等轮廓错误字形的情况下点击导出，构建被阻断、不生成 OTF 文件，并提示轮廓错误及对应字形标识。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 检查通过后输出 OTF
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 在完整性检查无阻断性问题的项目中点击导出，系统生成可下载的 OTF 字体文件（文件名以 .otf 结尾且文件大小非零）。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 字符覆盖表内容正确
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 查看成功导出的字符覆盖表，其按所选字符集逐项列出字符及其是否已包含字形，已覆盖字符数与项目中实际入库字形数一致。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 字偶距清单内容正确
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 先为指定字符对建立一条字偶距规则并记录数值，成功导出后查看字偶距清单，其中包含该字符对及其设定数值。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 问题报告内容正确
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 在保留至少一个非阻断性问题（如尺寸离群或缺失字符）的情况下导出并查看问题报告，报告列出该问题的类型与对应字形/字符标识，与字体指标页的检测结果一致。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 项目数据跨会话保存
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 完成字形编辑、指标修改与一条字偶距规则创建后刷新页面并重新进入项目，修改后的字形、指标数值、字偶距规则与版本历史条目均与刷新前一致。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 原始样本跨会话保存
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 上传样张扫描图并完成切分后刷新页面并重新进入项目，原始扫描样本仍可在样张列表中查看，并可基于该原始样本再次执行重新校准。

verification_guideline:
总体顺序（后置检查点依赖前置产物，请严格按此骨架推进，不要跳步）：
1) 先进入「字符集/模板」，选择一个字符数足以跨页的字符集（若有多选/范围勾选，尽量选到几十个以上字符），记录界面显示的字符集名称与字符数；再执行「下载/生成模板」，在应用内预览或打开生成的 PDF，逐页查看页数、格位编号、基线与定位点标记。若模板以新标签/下载形式产出，优先在应用内预览页查看；确实只能下载时，记录文件名与页数提示信息。
2) 再进入「上传与切分」，按顺序上传 fixtures 中的样张：先上传正常样张 handwriting_sheet_normal，再上传倾斜/透视变形样张 handwriting_sheet_skewed，最后上传包含空白格、潦草不可识别格、笔画越界格与孤立噪点的样张 handwriting_sheet_edgecases。每张上传后都要触发处理/切分动作（有独立的「处理」「校正」「切分」按钮时需显式点击），并在处理完成后再进行下一张。
3) 若上传或切分存在进度条、排队或模拟耗时，先确认任务已启动，再使用 advance_time 推进时间，不要在任务尚未启动时提前推进。
4) 在做切分数量与队列相关观察前，先记录关键基线数值：本页样张的格位总数 N、成功入库字形数、待处理队列条目数、版本历史当前条目数。后续每次操作后再回读同一批数值做对比。
5) 重复映射场景：如应用不会自动产生，可在切分结果或队列中手动把某个字形的 Unicode 指派成与另一字形相同的码位（或使用应用提供的「指派/重映射」入口）来构造冲突；越界与无法识别场景优先由 handwriting_sheet_edgecases 触发。处理队列条目时，先记录该条目的格位编号，出队后到正式字形库中按该编号确认。
6) 字形编辑器相关操作（去噪、拖动控制点、字宽、基线、左右边距、锚点）：先在画布或目标控件上单击使其获得焦点，再执行拖动或键盘输入；数值类字段修改后务必点击「应用/保存」。设定数值时使用便于识别的独特值（如字宽 723、行距 1234、字偶距 -137），避免与内置示例数据混淆。修改轮廓/字宽后，重新打开该字形确认是否保留。
7) 复合字形链路：先确保至少存在两个已入库的基础字形，再新建复合字形并引用它们；随后回到其中一个基础字形修改轮廓或字宽并保存，再切回复合字形与预览区观察，不要通过刷新页面来代替同步观察。
8) 字体指标与自动检测：先保存 UPM/升部/降部/行距与至少两个字符组的视觉中心，再故意制造用于检测的异常（自交轮廓、明显偏离的字宽、明显偏移的基线、造成重叠的边距），然后运行一次自动检测并完整浏览结果列表；保留其中至少一个非阻断性问题（如尺寸离群或缺失字符）用于后续问题报告核对。
9) 字偶距与样文：先记录样文预览中目标字符对的当前视觉间距（截图对照），再新建规则并填明显负值保存，回到同一样文位置对比；混排碰撞检测需在含多段中西文的样文上运行，并检查结果是否能定位到具体字符对与位置。
10) 版本历史：分别执行「重新校准某页样张」「替换某个字形」「修改 UPM 或行距」三类操作，每次操作后立刻回版本历史记录条目数与新条目标注；确保累计至少 3 个版本后再对最早版本执行「恢复」，恢复后再次记录条目数与列表内容。同时留意界面是否提供覆盖/删除历史版本的入口。
11) 导出需做两轮：第一轮在仍保留无效映射（重复映射或未指派 Unicode）与轮廓错误字形的状态下点击导出，观察检查流程与阻断表现；第二轮再清理这些阻断性问题（处理队列、修复轮廓）后重新导出，查看是否产出 OTF 及字符覆盖表、字偶距清单、问题报告，并把覆盖表数量、清单中的字偶距数值与前面记录的数值逐一比对。
12) 持久化检查放在最后：完成字形编辑、指标修改与字偶距规则创建后再刷新/重新进入项目，核对字形、指标、字偶距、版本历史与原始样张是否一致，并确认可基于原始样本再次执行重新校准。刷新仅用于此项持久化验证。
13) 区分空状态与缺失功能：模板未生成前的空模板区、未上传前的空样张列表、未产生问题时的空检测结果，属于正常空态；只有在按上述步骤产出数据后仍无对应区域或入口，才视为功能缺失。若某入口只提供内置示例数据（如「载入示例样张」）而不接受真实文件上传，需明确记录这一事实。

fixtures.name: handwriting_sheet_normal
fixtures.purpose: 用于上传扫描样张、切分入库、字形关联信息、切分结果进入编辑器等检查点
fixtures.suggested_content: 模拟一张已填写完成的手写字模模板扫描件：白色纸张背景，正视无变形。页面顶部有页码标注（如 P01），四角各有一个实心黑色方形定位点标记。中部为 4 行 × 5 列共 20 个正方形浅灰细线书写格，每格右上角或格外有小号格位编号文字（如 P01-R01-C01 …… P01-R04-C05），每格中间有一条浅灰水平虚线作为基线。每个格内用黑色毛笔/钢笔风格写有一个规整的常用汉字（如 一、二、三、人、大、小、上、下、中、日、月、山、水、火、木、金、土、天、地、心），笔画完整、居中、不超出格线。分辨率约 1240×1754（A4 150dpi 比例），无需 EXIF/GPS。

fixtures.name: handwriting_sheet_skewed
fixtures.purpose: 用于按页透视校正、重新校准与版本生成相关检查点
fixtures.suggested_content: 与 handwriting_sheet_normal 同版式的第二页样张（页码标注 P02，格位编号 P02-R01-C01 起），但整页明显倾斜并带透视变形：纸张顺时针旋转约 8 度，且上边比下边窄（梯形透视），四角黑色方形定位点随之偏移成不规则四边形，纸面有轻微灰度阴影与扫描噪点。格内写有另外 20 个常用汉字（如 人、口、手、目、耳、田、力、刀、马、鸟、鱼、虫、石、玉、米、禾、竹、车、门、雨），笔画清晰但整体随页面倾斜。白底黑字，分辨率约 1240×1754，无需 EXIF/GPS。

title: VanillaPad Build Lab
query: 我是前端工程师，想做一个在浏览器中完成模块分析、增量构建和回归验证的 Web App「VanillaPad Build Lab」。用户可新建项目或导入 ZIP，文件树支持 HTML、CSS、JavaScript 与静态资源；系统解析 import、export、CSS 引用和入口关系，生成可交互的模块依赖图，缺失模块、循环依赖、重复导出和路径大小写冲突必须定位到文件与行。项目可建立 development、test、production 三套构建配置，分别设置入口、环境变量、资源内联阈值和代码分包规则；环境变量缺失或生产配置引用测试资源时阻止构建。修改文件后只重新构建其反向依赖闭包，并显示缓存命中、失效模块、构建耗时与产物体积变化，不能每次伪装成全量成功。预览在隔离环境运行，控制台把语法错误、运行异常和资源失败映射回源码。用户可创建带固定输入和 DOM 断言的回归用例，同一用例需在两个构建版本上运行并比较结果、错误和页面快照摘要。每次成功构建保存文件哈希、配置、依赖图和产物清单，恢复历史版本必须产生新构建。最终导出源码 ZIP、产物包、依赖清单和构建报告；同名文件导入、配置变更及失败构建均保留审计记录，项目状态跨会话保存。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 新建空白项目
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 通过“新建项目”入口创建项目后，项目被打开并显示可编辑的文件树结构。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 导入 ZIP 生成项目
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 导入一个包含多个文件的 ZIP 后，压缩包内的目录与文件按原层级出现在文件树中并可打开查看内容。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 文件树支持四类文件
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 文件树可展示并打开 HTML、CSS、JavaScript 以及图片等静态资源文件，缺少任一类型即判定失败。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 解析依赖关系生成模块依赖图
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 对含 import/export、CSS 引用（如 @import 或 link）及入口文件的项目执行分析后，依赖图按真实引用关系渲染出模块节点与有向连线。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 依赖图可交互
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 在依赖图中点击或选中某个模块节点后，该节点及其上下游连线被高亮或展示该模块的依赖详情。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 缺失模块定位到文件与行
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 当某文件 import 了不存在的模块时，问题列表报告“缺失模块”并给出引用它的源文件路径与行号。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 循环依赖定位到文件与行
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 构造 A→B→A 的相互引用后，问题列表报告“循环依赖”并列出环路上各文件的路径与引用行号。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 重复导出定位到文件与行
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 同一模块中导出两个同名符号（或多个模块重复导出同一符号）时，问题列表报告“重复导出”并给出文件路径与行号。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 路径大小写冲突定位到文件与行
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 当引用路径与实际文件名大小写不一致（如 import './Utils.js' 而文件为 utils.js）时，问题列表报告“路径大小写冲突”并给出引用文件路径与行号。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 创建 development/test/production 三套构建配置
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 可分别为 development、test、production 三种环境建立独立配置，并在每套配置中设置入口文件、环境变量、资源内联阈值和代码分包规则，四项设置均被保存且互不覆盖。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 环境变量缺失时阻止构建
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 当所选配置引用了未定义的环境变量时，点击构建被拒绝执行并提示缺失的变量名，不产生成功构建记录。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 生产配置引用测试资源时阻止构建
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: production 配置的入口或依赖中包含测试用资源/文件时，构建被拒绝执行并提示违规引用的具体文件。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 仅重建修改文件的反向依赖闭包
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 首次完整构建后修改某个文件并再次构建，重建的模块集合恰为该文件及其反向依赖闭包内的模块，闭包外模块不被重建。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 展示增量构建指标
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 每次构建后展示缓存命中情况、失效模块列表、构建耗时以及产物体积变化四项信息，缺少任一项即判定失败。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 构建指标随实际修改变化而非伪装全量成功
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 未修改任何文件重复构建时缓存命中率显著提高且失效模块为空，修改不同范围文件后失效模块数与耗时随之变化，而不是每次显示相同的全量成功结果。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 预览在隔离环境运行
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 构建产物在沙箱化的 iframe 或 Worker 等隔离环境中运行，预览页面的脚本错误不会中断或污染主应用界面。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 语法错误与运行异常映射回源码
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 在源文件中制造语法错误或运行时抛出异常后，控制台条目显示对应的源文件路径与行号，而非仅显示打包产物的位置。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 资源加载失败映射回引用位置
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 预览中引用不存在的图片或样式等资源时，控制台记录该资源加载失败并指出发起引用的源文件与行号。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 创建带固定输入与 DOM 断言的回归用例
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 可新建回归用例并填写固定输入与 DOM 断言（如选择器与期望文本/属性），保存后用例出现在用例列表中且内容可再次查看。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 同一用例在两个构建版本上运行
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 选择同一回归用例并指定两个不同的构建版本后执行，系统分别在两个版本的产物上运行该用例并给出各自的断言结果。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 对比两版本的结果、错误与快照摘要
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 两个版本运行完成后展示对比视图，逐项列出断言结果差异、错误信息差异和页面快照摘要差异，两版本行为不同时能标出差异项。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 成功构建保存完整版本快照
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 每次构建成功后历史列表新增一条记录，其详情包含文件哈希、所用构建配置、依赖图和产物清单四类信息。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 恢复历史版本产生新构建
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 对某条历史记录执行恢复后，文件与配置回到该版本状态，并新增一条时间更新的构建记录，而不是直接复用或覆盖被恢复的旧记录。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 导出源码 ZIP、产物包、依赖清单与构建报告
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 可分别导出源码 ZIP、构建产物包、依赖清单和构建报告四种文件，且各导出内容与当前项目的文件、产物、依赖关系和最近构建结果一致，缺少任一项即判定失败。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 记录同名文件导入、配置变更与失败构建
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 导入与已有文件同名的文件、修改构建配置、以及构建失败后，审计记录中分别新增对应条目并带有时间与操作对象描述，缺少任一类事件即判定失败。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 项目状态跨会话保存
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 刷新页面或关闭后重新打开应用，项目文件树内容、三套构建配置、构建历史与回归用例仍保持关闭前的状态。

verification_guideline:
总体顺序建议：先建项目并落地文件 → 依赖分析与问题定位 → 三套构建配置 → 基线构建与增量构建 → 预览/控制台 → 回归用例（需已有两个构建版本）→ 历史与恢复 → 导出 → 审计 → 最后刷新验证持久化。多数检查点依赖“至少一次成功构建”，请勿跳过基线构建。

1) 起步：先用“新建项目”入口创建一个空白项目（记录初始是否为空状态；空列表/空图不等于功能缺失）。随后再用提供的 ZIP 夹具执行一次导入，确认目录层级与各文件能打开查看内容。若应用只支持二选一（新建或导入），两条路径都尝试一次并记录实际行为。

2) 文件类型覆盖：确保项目中同时存在 HTML、CSS、JavaScript 与图片静态资源四类文件（ZIP 夹具已含；若导入后缺图片，用单独的 PNG 夹具再上传一次），逐类点开确认可展示/可打开。

3) 命名唯一性：所有自行新建的文件、配置名、回归用例名、变量名均带唯一标记（如 VP048_<两位分钟数>），便于与应用自带示例数据区分；截图前先记录该标记。

4) 依赖分析：先在“未注入错误”的干净状态下执行一次分析，观察依赖图节点与有向连线是否与真实 import/export、CSS 引用、入口关系一致；再点击/选中某个节点观察高亮或依赖详情。

5) 四类问题需分别、逐个注入并重新分析，每次注入后记录问题列表中显示的问题类型、文件路径与行号（不要一次性注入全部导致互相掩盖）：①引用不存在的模块；②构造 A→B→A 互相引用；③同一模块或跨模块重复导出同名符号；④引用路径与真实文件名大小写不一致。验证完成后把这些错误改回可用状态，再进入构建环节。

6) 构建配置：分别建立 development、test、production 三套配置，每套都填写入口文件、环境变量、资源内联阈值、代码分包规则四项，并使用不同取值；切换配置来回查看，确认各自取值未被覆盖。修改配置的动作会被审计检查点复用，请记录修改时间点与被改对象。

7) 阻止构建的两个负向场景需在已有可成功构建的基线之后单独制造：①让所选配置引用一个未定义的环境变量并点击构建；②让 production 配置的入口或依赖链上包含明显的测试用资源（例如带 test/spec 命名的文件）并点击构建。每次记录提示内容，并检查构建历史是否新增了“成功”记录。验证完成后恢复合法配置。

8) 增量构建取证顺序（关键）：先做一次完整构建并记录耗时/缓存/产物体积；不修改任何文件立即再构建一次并记录；然后修改一个处于依赖链末端（反向依赖少）的文件构建一次；再修改一个被多处引用的公共模块构建一次。四次的失效模块列表、缓存命中、耗时、产物体积变化需逐次截图对比，不要只看最后一次结果。

9) 预览与控制台：先确认预览确实在隔离容器中运行（可观察预览崩溃时主界面是否仍可操作）。再分别制造三类问题各一次并观察控制台条目中显示的源文件与行号：语法错误、运行时抛出异常、引用不存在的图片或样式资源。逐项验证后立即还原源码，避免影响后续构建与回归。

10) 回归验证前提：必须先在同一项目上产生至少两个可选择的成功构建版本（例如在两次构建之间小幅修改会影响 DOM 输出的代码，使两版本行为存在可见差异）。之后再创建带固定输入与 DOM 断言（选择器 + 期望文本/属性）的用例，保存后回到列表确认可再次查看内容，然后选择同一用例分别在这两个版本上运行并查看对比视图。

11) 历史与恢复：在历史记录详情中逐项查找文件哈希、所用配置、依赖图、产物清单；执行“恢复”后，记录文件/配置是否回到旧状态，并检查历史列表条目数量与时间戳的变化（恢复前后各截一张历史列表）。

12) 导出四类产物（源码 ZIP、产物包、依赖清单、构建报告）需分别触发并记录下载结果；若能查看导出内容，抽查其是否包含前面用唯一标记命名的文件与最近一次构建信息。

13) 审计记录集中在导出之后查看：确认前面已完成的三类事件（导入同名文件、修改构建配置、构建失败）各自对应的条目，注意“同名文件导入”需要使用与项目中已有文件同名的夹具再导入一次来触发。

14) 最后做持久化：刷新页面（或关闭标签页重新打开）后，逐一回看文件树、三套配置、构建历史与回归用例是否保持刷新前的内容与唯一标记。刷新仅用于持久化验证，不得替代其他检查点的即时观察。

title: 拥塞实验室
query: 我是网络协议研究者，想做一个确定性离散事件模拟 Web App「拥塞实验室」，比较 BBRv3、CUBIC 与自定义简化算法在相同流量下的行为。用户配置链路带宽、传播时延、队列策略、缓冲区、随机丢包、流数量、起止时间和固定随机种子；系统按发送、入队、确认、丢包、超时与重传事件推进虚拟时钟，而不是用随机动画冒充模拟。每条流保存拥塞窗口、在途字节、RTT、吞吐量和状态阶段，点击任一时间点可回放导致该状态的事件链与计算公式。模拟过程中持续校验“已发送字节＝已确认＋已丢弃＋仍在途”等守恒关系，出现负窗口、重复确认或事件乱序时将本次运行标为无效。用户可复制场景只替换算法，比较吞吐量、P95 排队时延、丢包率、Jain 公平性、收敛时间和饥饿区间；还可对两个参数设置范围批量扫描，生成结果矩阵并打开任一单元格对应的完整运行。修改参数后以同一种子重算，历史结果不得覆盖。长时间运行可对图表降采样，但统计必须基于完整事件。场景、运行、种子、事件日志与比较报告跨会话保存，最终导出事件 CSV、配置 JSON、指标摘要和可复现实验编号，非法参数组合需在运行前阻断并说明原因。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 主功能区入口齐全
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 应用主界面存在全局导航（顶栏或侧栏），包含「场景配置/运行」「运行详情与事件回放」「算法比较」「参数扫描」「历史记录」五类功能入口。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 导航可切换至比较与扫描视图
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 依次点击导航中的「算法比较」与「参数扫描」入口，主内容区分别切换为比较报告视图与参数扫描配置/矩阵视图。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 场景配置项齐全
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 场景配置区可配置链路带宽、传播时延、队列策略、缓冲区大小、随机丢包率、流数量、仿真起始时间、仿真结束时间与固定随机种子，缺任一项即不通过。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 拥塞算法可选 BBRv3/CUBIC/自定义
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 算法选择控件至少提供 BBRv3、CUBIC 与自定义简化算法三个可选项。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 配置后可执行模拟并产出运行结果
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 填入带宽 10 Mbps、时延 20 ms、队列策略 FIFO、缓冲区 100 KB、丢包率 0.1%、流数量 2、0–10 s、种子 42、算法 CUBIC 后点击运行，模拟完成并生成一条运行记录且展示该次运行的指标或流状态曲线。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 双参数范围批量扫描生成结果矩阵

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 改参重算不覆盖历史结果

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 场景、运行、种子与事件日志跨会话保存

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 比较报告跨会话保存
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 生成一份两次运行的比较报告后刷新页面重新进入应用，该报告仍可被找回且展示与刷新前一致的指标数值。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 导出事件 CSV

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 导出配置 JSON 与界面配置一致
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 以带宽 10 Mbps、时延 20 ms、缓冲区 100 KB、流数量 2、种子 42 运行后导出配置 JSON，其带宽、传播时延、队列策略、缓冲区、丢包率、流数量、起止时间与随机种子字段取值与界面配置完全一致。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 导出指标摘要
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 对一次已完成的运行导出指标摘要，文件中包含吞吐量、P95 排队时延、丢包率、Jain 公平性、收敛时间与饥饿区间数值，且与界面所示同一运行的指标一致。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 可复现实验编号
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 完成一次运行后界面显示非空的可复现实验编号，其值与导出的配置或摘要文件中记录的编号一致，且该编号在历史中可唯一定位到该次运行。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 长运行图表降采样呈现
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 执行一次长时间运行（如 0–120 s、上万事件）后查看流状态曲线，曲线以明显少于事件总数的降采样数据点渲染且横轴仍覆盖完整 0–120 s，页面可正常交互。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 统计基于完整事件而非降采样点
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 对同一长时间运行导出事件 CSV 并按其中丢包与发送事件数计算丢包率，界面/指标摘要显示的丢包率与该完整事件计算结果一致（允许 1% 误差）。

verification_guideline:
本应用是自建的离散事件模拟工具，初次进入很可能为空状态（无场景、无运行、无比较报告、无扫描矩阵）。看到空列表并附有「新建场景 / 开始运行」等入口，只说明尚无数据，不等于功能缺失；必须先自己创建数据再判断。

1. 先做全局巡览：进入后先在顶栏/侧栏逐个点开各功能入口（场景配置与运行、运行详情与事件回放、算法比较、参数扫描、历史记录），记录入口名称与切换后主内容区的变化，再开始具体操作。此步是导航类检查点的唯一依据，不要用「猜测入口存在」代替实际点击。

2. 建立基线运行 A（后续绝大多数检查点都依赖它）：在场景配置中逐项填写并截图确认已生效——链路带宽 10 Mbps、传播时延 20 ms、队列策略 FIFO、缓冲区 100 KB、随机丢包率 0.1%、流数量 2、仿真 0–10 s、随机种子 42、算法 CUBIC，然后运行。运行若为异步（有进度条/「运行中」状态），要等待其自行完成后再截图，不要在未完成状态下判定结果；不要用 advance_time 推进模拟（虚拟时钟由引擎推进，不是真实计时器）。

3. 建议给每个场景起带唯一标记的名称（如「S1-049-A-42」「S1-049-B-20M」等短标记），便于在历史列表、比较报告、扫描矩阵和导出文件中确认看到的是本次创建的数据，而非应用自带的示例数据。

4. 事件与守恒相关检查点需要另一次更易产生丢包/重传的运行：在基线基础上把丢包率改为 1%（其余参数与种子 42 保持不变）再运行，然后在运行详情中打开事件日志、守恒/统计面板与有效性区域。事件日志若分页或虚拟滚动，需翻页或用筛选/类型过滤逐类查看，并记录事件总条数（后续与导出 CSV 行数比对时要用同一次运行）。

5. 确定性检查：用完全相同的参数与种子 42 再运行一次，逐项抄录两次运行的事件总数与关键指标数值后再比较；比较时务必确认是两条不同的运行记录，而不是同一条记录被重复打开。

6. 回放检查有严格顺序：先在某条流的曲线/时序上读取并抄录选定时间点的拥塞窗口与在途字节数值，再点击该时间点打开回放面板，比对事件链与末态数值。若曲线不可直接点击，尝试时间轴滑块、时序表行点击或事件日志中的「定位到该时刻」等等价入口，并在记录中说明使用了哪种入口。

7. 算法比较顺序：先用「复制场景并替换算法」把基线场景复制为 BBRv3 并运行，逐项核对新运行的各配置字段与原场景是否只有算法不同；再选取这两次运行生成比较报告，逐项抄录报告中的六类指标数值。另需单独运行一次流数量＝1 的场景，以及一次带宽 10 Mbps、缓冲区 100 KB、4 条流的明显排队场景，用于公平性与 P95 排队时延的核算（后者需回到该运行的事件日志/排队时延数据自行核算分位数）。

8. 参数扫描：在扫描视图分别为带宽设置 {5,10,20} Mbps、为缓冲区设置 {50,100} KB（注意区分「离散取值列表」与「起止+步长」两种输入方式，按界面实际形式填写并截图确认），启动后等待全部组合完成，再检查矩阵行列标签与单元格数值，然后点击带宽 20 / 缓冲区 50 的单元格进入其完整运行详情核对配置与可查看内容。

9. 历史不覆盖检查：先抄录运行 A 的参数与吞吐量等指标，再仅把带宽改为 20 Mbps（种子仍为 42）重新运行，随后回到历史列表同时打开 A 与新运行 B 逐项比对，确认 A 的数值未被改写。

10. 持久化检查放在其它操作基本完成之后：在同一标签页刷新或关闭后重新打开应用，回到历史列表核对场景、运行记录、种子显示、事件日志条数与已生成的比较报告是否仍与刷新前一致（刷新前请先记录这些具体数值）。刷新仅用于持久化验证，不要用它替代其它功能的观察。

11. 导出：对同一次已完成运行依次导出事件 CSV、配置 JSON、指标摘要，并尽量在浏览器中打开/预览下载文件的实际内容，核对表头、字段取值、数据行数以及可复现实验编号是否与界面显示一致；若环境无法打开文件，至少记录下载成功的提示与文件名，并在结论中说明未能读取内容。

12. 长运行与降采样：单独执行一次 0–120 s（可保持其余参数、种子不变）的运行，等待完成后观察曲线的数据点密度与横轴覆盖范围，并对该次运行导出事件 CSV，用其中发送与丢包事件数自行核算丢包率再与界面指标比对。长运行期间若页面卡顿，需等待其结束而不是中途刷新。

13. 非法参数阻断放在最后做，且做完后务必把参数改回合法值：分别尝试结束时间早于起始时间（起始 10 s、结束 5 s）与丢包率 150%，点击运行后既要看提示文案是否指明具体非法项与原因，也要回到历史列表确认是否新增了运行记录。

title: TraceTwin PCB 协同设计台
query:
构建「TraceTwin PCB 协同设计台」，一个用于完成小型电路板布局、布线与装配校核的 Web App。工作区左右联动：左侧为按毫米标尺绘制的二维 PCB，显示板框、焊盘、过孔、网络飞线及红色顶层／蓝色底层走线；右侧为可旋转、缩放和剖切的三维电路板，真实呈现芯片、接口、按键、电容和不同高度的元件。任一视图选中或移动元件，另一侧必须同步高亮并更新位置、朝向和标号。

内置一块双层控制板及完整网络表。用户可拖动元件、锁定关键接口、绘制45度线段、切换层并放置过孔；走线必须吸附到正确焊盘，实时显示所属网络、线宽、总长度和未完成连接。差分对要求保持设定间距并计算长度偏差，电源网络根据电流规则限制最小线宽。移动已布线元件时不能直接断开连接，而要让用户选择推挤周围走线、保留铜线并生成待修复端点，或撤销移动。

设计规则检查须定位短路、跨网误连、间距不足、走线穿越禁布区、过孔超出板框、悬空网络及丝印压住焊盘等问题；点击问题要同时在二维与三维视图定位。三维装配检查还需载入一个半透明外壳，检测元件高度超限、接口方向错误、元件相互穿插和螺丝柱碰撞，并显示最小剩余间隙。内置三处故障供直接修复；每次修改只重算受影响网络和碰撞体。支持撤销重做，最终输出分层布线摘要、未解决问题清单和带坐标的元件装配表。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 左右联动双视图工作区存在
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 打开应用后，界面同时存在左侧二维 PCB 绘图区与右侧三维电路板视图区，二者并排可见且各自渲染出板卡内容。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 内置双层控制板与完整网络表
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 打开应用即已载入预置的双层控制板（含元件、焊盘与顶/底两层），且网络表面板列出该板的全部网络名称，网络条目与板上元件引脚相对应。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 二维视图绘制毫米标尺、板框、焊盘与过孔
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 二维 PCB 视图中同时可辨认出带毫米刻度（标注 mm）的标尺、板框轮廓、元件焊盘与过孔四类图元。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 未布线网络显示飞线
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 二维视图中，属于同一网络但尚未布线连通的焊盘之间显示网络飞线（细线/虚线），并可与已布线走线区分。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 切换当前走线层生效
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 将当前工作层由顶层切换为底层后，层指示器显示当前层为底层，且此后绘制的新走线被标记并渲染为底层走线。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 放置过孔实现跨层连接
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 使用过孔工具在一段已有走线端点处放置过孔后，该位置出现过孔图元，且走线可从该点切换到另一层继续绘制形成跨层连接。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 顶层红色、底层蓝色走线区分
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 二维视图中顶层走线以红色渲染、底层走线以蓝色渲染，两层走线颜色可明确区分。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 三维电路板与元件渲染
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 右侧三维视图中渲染出立体电路板本体及其上的元件模型，可在画布中直接观察到板面与元件。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 三维视图可旋转与缩放
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 在三维视图中拖动可使相机视角明显旋转，滚轮或缩放控件可放大/缩小板卡显示尺寸。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 三维剖切功能
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 开启剖切并调整剖切面位置后，板卡沿剖切面被截断显示可见内部或元件截面，关闭剖切后恢复完整模型。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 三维元件形态与类型一致
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 三维视图中芯片、接口、按键、电容分别呈现可区分的外形且元件高度不同，不得所有元件均为同一尺寸的方块占位体。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 二维选中同步高亮三维
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 在二维视图中点击选中某元件后，三维视图中对应的同一元件立即高亮显示，其他元件保持未高亮。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 三维选中同步高亮二维
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 在三维视图中点击选中某元件后，二维视图中对应的同一元件立即高亮显示。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 拖动元件位置跨视图同步
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 在二维视图中拖动某未锁定元件到新坐标后，该元件在二维画布停留于新位置且坐标读数更新，三维视图中同一元件同步移动到相对应的新位置。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 元件朝向跨视图同步

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 两视图元件标号一致
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 选中任一元件后，二维视图与三维视图（或其信息面板）显示的元件标号为同一位号字符串（如均为 U1）。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 锁定关键接口后禁止移动
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 对某接口类元件执行锁定后再拖动该元件，元件位置保持不变并给出锁定提示或拒绝移动的可见反馈。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 走线吸附到正确焊盘
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 从某网络焊盘起笔并在目标焊盘附近（未精确点中）结束绘制时，走线端点被吸附到该目标焊盘中心，且走线归属网络与两端焊盘所属网络一致。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 实时显示走线所属网络与线宽

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 网络总长度计算

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 未完成连接数实时更新
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 记录当前未完成连接数量 N，完成一条飞线对应的布线后，未完成连接数量变为 N-1 且该飞线从二维视图消失。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 差分对保持设定间距
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 为一对差分网络设定间距（如 0.2 mm）并绘制走线后，两条走线在平行段保持该设定间距，偏离设定值时给出可见的间距违规提示。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 差分对长度偏差计算
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 绘制一对长度明显不等的差分走线后，面板显示的长度偏差数值等于两条走线总长度之差（允许显示精度误差）。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 电源网络最小线宽限制

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 保留铜线并生成待修复端点
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 移动已布线元件并选择“保留铜线并生成待修复端点”后，原铜线仍保留在画布上，二维视图中生成标记的待修复端点，且该端点作为条目出现在未解决问题清单中。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 撤销移动恢复原状
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 记录已布线元件原坐标后拖动并选择“撤销移动”，该元件回到移动前坐标且其相关走线形状与移动前一致。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: DRC 检查入口与问题清单存在
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 工作区中存在设计规则检查面板，可触发检查并以列表形式展示带问题类型描述的问题条目。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 短路检测
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 绘制走线使两个不同网络的焊盘直接连通并运行 DRC 后，问题清单新增“短路”类型问题并指明涉及的两个网络。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 跨网误连检测
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 将某网络走线端点连接到不属于该网络的焊盘并运行 DRC 后，问题清单出现“跨网误连”类型问题并标明该走线与错误焊盘。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 间距不足检测
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 将两条不同网络的走线绘制到小于规则间距的距离并运行 DRC 后，问题清单出现“间距不足”类型问题并给出实际间距与规则值。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 走线穿越禁布区检测
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 绘制一段走线穿过板上禁布区并运行 DRC 后，问题清单出现“走线穿越禁布区”类型问题并指向该走线。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 过孔超出板框检测
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 在板框边界之外放置一个过孔并运行 DRC 后，问题清单出现“过孔超出板框”类型问题并指向该过孔。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 悬空网络检测
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 删除某网络中一段走线使其存在未连通的铜线或未连接引脚并运行 DRC 后，问题清单出现“悬空网络”类型问题并标明该网络名称。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 丝印压住焊盘检测
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 移动某元件丝印/位号使其覆盖到焊盘上并运行 DRC 后，问题清单出现“丝印压住焊盘”类型问题并指向该丝印与焊盘。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 点击问题在二维与三维同时定位
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 点击问题清单中任一条目后，二维视图与三维视图同时定位到该问题对应的图元/区域并高亮显示，两侧指向同一对象。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 载入半透明外壳
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 执行载入外壳/装配校核后，三维场景中出现包裹电路板的外壳模型且以半透明方式渲染，透过外壳仍可看到内部板卡与元件。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 将较高元件置于外壳内高度受限区域并运行装配检查后，装配问题清单出现“元件高度超限”类型问题并标明该元件位号与超出量。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 将某接口元件旋转到与外壳开孔不匹配的朝向并运行装配检查后，装配问题清单出现“接口方向错误”类型问题并指向该接口元件。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 元件相互穿插检测
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 将两个元件移动到彼此三维体积重叠的位置并运行装配检查后，装配问题清单出现“元件相互穿插/干涉”类型问题并列出涉及的两个元件位号。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 螺丝柱碰撞检测
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 将某元件移动到外壳螺丝柱所在位置并运行装配检查后，装配问题清单出现“螺丝柱碰撞”类型问题并指向该元件与对应螺丝柱。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 最小剩余间隙数值
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 运行装配检查后界面显示带毫米单位的最小剩余间隙数值，且将某元件移动到更贴近外壳的位置后该数值相应减小。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 内置三处可修复故障
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 打开应用并运行检查后，问题清单中包含三处预置故障条目，每条均标明问题类型与所在对象。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 修复故障后问题清单更新
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 修复其中一处内置故障（如加宽线宽、移开丝印或重连走线）后重新检查，该故障条目从问题清单中移除、问题总数减少 1，其余两处故障仍保留。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 仅重算受影响网络与碰撞体
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 移动一个只与少数网络相连的元件后，系统给出的重算范围（重算网络列表/受影响碰撞体）仅包含与该元件相连的网络及邻近碰撞体，未涉及网络的长度与问题结果保持不变。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 撤销恢复上一步操作
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 绘制一段新走线后点击撤销，该段走线从二维视图消失，网络总长度与未完成连接计数恢复到绘制前的数值。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 重做恢复被撤销操作
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 绘制一段走线后先撤销再点击重做，该段走线重新出现且形状与网络归属与撤销前一致。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 分层布线摘要输出
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 完成至少一段顶层与一段底层走线后生成输出，分层布线摘要按顶层/底层分别列出走线长度或段数统计值，且与当前设计中各层实际走线情况一致。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 未解决问题清单输出
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 在存在未修复问题的状态下生成输出，未解决问题清单条目与当前 DRC/装配问题面板中的未解决问题在数量与类型上一一对应。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 元件装配表含标号与坐标
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 生成输出后，元件装配表逐行列出板上每个元件的标号及其 X/Y 坐标（含毫米单位），行数与板上元件数量一致。

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: 移动元件后装配表坐标更新
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: 记录某元件在装配表中的坐标，将其在二维视图中沿 X 方向移动约 5 mm 后重新生成输出，装配表中该元件坐标按移动方向相应变化并与二维视图新坐标一致。

verification_guideline:
本查询为单会话、纯前端 PCB 设计工具，无需登录、无需外部素材；所有验证均在同一页面内完成。以下顺序旨在减少重复评测间的差异。

1) 先做只读观察，再做破坏性操作。进入应用后不要立刻拖动或布线：先完整截图记录初始状态——左侧二维视图（标尺与 mm 刻度、板框、焊盘、过孔、飞线、顶/底层走线配色）、右侧三维视图（板体与不同高度元件外形）、网络表面板中的网络列表、DRC/装配问题面板与其中的预置故障条目数量与类型。把初始的“未完成连接数”“各网络长度”“问题总数”抄写下来，后续多个数值型检查点都以这些基线作对照。

2) 熟悉工具与模式切换。先在工具栏/侧栏中定位：选择工具、布线工具、过孔工具、层切换（顶层/底层）、锁定、旋转、剖切开关、DRC 运行入口、装配校核/载入外壳入口、撤销/重做、生成报告入口。多数功能是模式化的：绘制走线、放置过孔、拖动元件互相排斥，每次操作前确认当前处于正确模式，操作后再切回选择模式，避免误触发其他工具导致后续步骤失败。

3) 依赖链要按序执行：
   - 层切换 → 再绘制新走线，才能观察新走线的层归属与配色；过孔跨层连接需先有一段走线端点存在。
   - 布线相关的“所属网络/线宽/网络总长度/未完成连接数/差分对偏差/电源最小线宽”都依赖成功画出至少一段走线；若首次绘制未成功（未起于焊盘或未闭合），先重试布线，再判断这些信息是否更新。
   - 差分对间距与长度偏差：先在设置/属性中指定差分对与间距值，再绘制两条走线。
   - 元件移动冲突三选项：必须选择一个“已经有走线连接”的元件来拖动，未布线元件通常不会触发冲突对话；三个选项（推挤／保留铜线生成待修复端点／撤销移动）需分三次独立的移动分别验证，每次验证后用撤销或反向移动恢复到接近基线的状态再做下一次。
   - 装配类检测（高度超限、接口方向错误、元件穿插、螺丝柱碰撞、最小剩余间隙）需先载入半透明外壳，再制造对应条件并重新运行装配检查。
   - 报告输出放在最后：先确保已存在至少一段顶层与一段底层走线、以及至少一个未解决问题，再生成报告，这样分层摘要、未解决问题清单、装配表三项可一次性观察。

4) 拖动与画布交互要点：在画布中拖动元件或绘制走线时，先在画布上单击使其获得焦点，再使用按下—移动—释放的连续拖拽（中途加入中间移动点），不要用单次瞬移点击；三维旋转/缩放同理，需在三维画布内拖拽与滚轮缩放，并对比拖拽前后的截图判断视角是否改变。绘制 45 度走线时，从焊盘中心起笔，向斜方向拖到明显偏离 45 度倍数的位置再释放，以观察角度约束是否生效。吸附检查时，终点故意落在目标焊盘附近但不精确命中。

5) 数值对照必须“先记录后比较”：任何涉及长度、偏差、未完成连接数、最小剩余间隙、问题计数、坐标的检查点，都要在操作前后各截一次图并读出具体数值再判断变化方向与量级；不要仅凭“看起来更新了”下结论。坐标类检查（装配表 vs 二维视图）要记录同一元件位号的移动前后坐标。

6) 故意制造 DRC 违规时使用可辨识的“新对象”：例如把新画的走线画到与另一网络焊盘相连、把两条不同网络走线画得极近、把走线穿过禁布区、把过孔放在板框外、删除某段走线制造悬空、移动丝印压住焊盘。每制造一种违规后立即运行一次 DRC 并记录问题清单快照，与上一次快照逐条比较，确认新增条目是本次操作产生而非初始预置故障。一次只制造一种违规，验证完再撤销/恢复，避免多种违规互相掩盖。

7) 内置故障与增量重算：预置故障应在初次运行检查时即出现；修复其中一处（按条目描述的方式，如加宽线宽、移开丝印、重连走线）后再次运行检查，比较问题总数与剩余条目。“仅重算受影响网络”需在移动元件后查看是否有重算范围/受影响网络提示，并核对未涉及网络的长度读数是否保持不变（因此移动前需先记录若干无关网络的长度）。

8) 联动与定位检查不要用刷新代替：二维选中→三维高亮、三维选中→二维高亮、拖动/旋转的跨视图同步、点击问题条目在两视图同时定位，都必须在同一次会话中即时观察两侧画面；每次点击后同时截取包含左右两个视图的完整界面截图作为证据。刷新页面可能重置设计状态，除非确需验证持久化，否则全程避免刷新或重新进入。

9) 撤销/重做在多步操作后容易受干扰：验证撤销与重做时，紧接在一次明确的绘制操作之后立即执行，不要中间插入其他操作；并在撤销前记录该网络长度与未完成连接数。

10) 区分“空态”与“功能缺失”：某些面板（如未解决问题清单、待修复端点列表、报告内容）在未触发对应操作前可能为空或提示“暂无”，这属于正常空态；只有在按上述前置步骤制造出数据后仍无更新，才作为功能问题记录。

11) 若某项交互（如剖切滑块、锁定后拖动、丝印移动）在界面上找不到直接入口，先尝试右键菜单、元件属性面板、双击元件、以及选中后出现的浮动工具条，再作出结论；并在截图中体现已尝试的入口位置。

title: OpenCloud
query: Build OpenCloud, a lightweight collaborative file workspace for a creator and up to 15 invited viewers who want to organize, share, review, and discuss project files in one place. Use platform-provided identity, invitations, file storage, database persistence, sharing permissions, and activity syncing. Use a clean document-management interface with a white background, deep teal branding, and four main areas: Files, Shared with Me, Activity, and Project Documentation. In Files, let users browse a folder tree, upload and download files, create folders, rename items, delete items when they have permission, search by file name, and open a detail panel showing owner, modified time, file size, and sharing status. The creator can assign each invited viewer read-only or editor permission for specific files or folders. Viewers can open shared files, comment on files when allowed, and see recent activity such as uploads, renames, edits, comments, permission changes, and deletions. Persist file metadata, folder structure, comments, permissions, and activity history through the platform data layer so the workspace survives refreshes and stays synced across participants. Enforce private files as owner-visible only and make permission-based actions clear in the UI. Add a Project Documentation area with README, Contributing, and More tabs for project metadata, license information, and contribution guidelines. Make the experience feel like a practical cloud file collaboration app powered by platform files and data capabilities.

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: Four main areas exist
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: The workspace exposes four reachable main areas: Files, Shared with Me, Activity, and Project Documentation.

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: Navigate to Activity
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: From the Files area, clicking the Activity entry switches the main view to the Activity area showing an activity/event list instead of the file browser.

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: Navigate to Project Documentation
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: From the Files area, clicking the Project Documentation entry switches the main view to the documentation area showing documentation tabs and content instead of the file browser.

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: White background with deep teal branding
atomic_functional_checkpoints.verification: The main workspace view uses a white background, and branding elements such as the logo, header, primary buttons, or the active navigation highlight use a deep teal color.

atomic_functional_checkpoints.checkpoint: Folder tree browsing

verification_guideline:
Use the four supplied files by their exact names. Complete each short check at its required state and reuse the resulting data; do not repeat the entire workflow for every AC. Identify created items by their app record IDs and exact filenames. Empty views before setup do not establish missing functionality.

1. Start in the platform-provided creator session. Visit Files, Shared with Me, Activity and Project Documentation. Check the navigation shell and white/deep-teal appearance. Confirm the displayed user identity; do not create app-specific accounts or invitation links as substitutes for platform identities.
2. Create 'Design Assets', enter it through the folder tree, and upload 'spec-notes.txt', 'budget.csv' and 'temp-delete.txt' one at a time. Upload 'private-plan.txt' in the creator's private root without sharing it or its parent. Record each upload's app item ID. Use the fixture path matching the selected file, not whichever file is first in the picker.
3. While 'spec-notes.txt' and 'budget.csv' are in the same visible scope, search 'spec', verify the inclusion/exclusion and clear the search. Open the spec file's detail panel and record owner, modified time, byte size and sharing status. Retrieve its platform-served content and download it; compare both with the actual supplied file, including 'OC-S051-SPEC-7K2M', the Page 2 section and the ending marker. A toast or filename alone does not prove stored or downloaded content.
4. Reload now, before renaming the folder, and verify that 'Design Assets' still contains the same 'spec-notes.txt' with its metadata. Check that its upload activity entry persists. Then rename 'Design Assets' to 'Design Assets v2' and verify the old name is absent. Delete only 'temp-delete.txt' through its action and confirmation, and verify its disappearance. Retain the private file and the spec file for later checks.
5. Use the platform invitation capability to add viewer_a. Observe the stated/enforced limit of 15; do not create 15 extra identities just to inspect the limit. Keep separate creator and viewer_a sessions. As creator, grant viewer_a read-only permission on 'spec-notes.txt'. In viewer_a, open Shared with Me, inspect the read-only label/actions, open the file and compare its content/metadata. Verify rename/delete are unavailable or rejected and the creator's file remains unchanged. Search for 'private-plan.txt' in the viewer's Files, Shared with Me and search results; it must remain owner-only.
6. Change that same spec file to editor permission. In viewer_a perform an actual supported edit, such as renaming it to 'spec-notes-edited.txt'; observe the same item change in the creator session. Restore the filename to 'spec-notes.txt' through the authorized UI before subsequent named-file checks. If a separate content-edit action exists, make and record a small visible edit for the edit activity event; do not count a rename as two distinct activity event types without evidence.
7. Where commenting is allowed, have viewer_a post exactly 'Please check page 2' on 'spec-notes.txt'. Record the new comment's ID/time and verify it in the creator's file thread and Activity feed with viewer_a attribution. Check the creator view before refreshing; if refresh is required, record that fact. Reload for comment persistence and verify the same comment remains.
8. Leave viewer_a with editor permission, reload the creator session and inspect that file's sharing panel. Inspect Activity after the required actions, using the recorded item IDs and actors to check upload, rename, edit, comment, permission-change and deletion events. Reuse earlier events instead of repeating the actions. An unperformed edit or an absent event is not proven by a generic activity list.
9. Finish by clicking README, Contributing and More and verifying their distinct project metadata, contribution guidelines and license content. If a prerequisite fails or a session cannot be provisioned, identify the affected checks and missing evidence; do not substitute seeded items or a single identity for the required operation.

title: chiron
query: Build chiron, a free open-source AI tutor web app for learners who want to study any topic at their own level and pace. Use platform-provided identity and database persistence so each learner has a durable personal Learning Vault. Start with a conversational intake that asks what the learner wants to learn, what they already know, how much time they have, and why they are learning it. Generate a personalized course path from the intake, making short goals such as a dinner-party crash course look clearly different from long goals such as a three-month mastery plan. The main workspace should include Course Path, Learning Session, and Learning Vault. Course Path shows milestones, prerequisite concepts, current progress, and the next recommended concept. Learning Session provides explanations, recall questions, quizzes, small practice tasks, examples, diagrams, and session summaries. Learning Vault stores notes, covered topics, strong areas, weak areas, saved materials, review plans, and prior session summaries for the current learner. Each new session should read from the learner’s Learning Vault, connect new ideas with past notes, adapt review questions to weak areas, and update the Vault after exercises are completed. Use platform AI capabilities for course generation, explanations, question design, summarization, and review planning. Keep each platform identity’s Learning Vault isolated. Use a calm document-style visual design with numbered sections, clear progress cues, concise input boxes, and visible continuity from intake to course path, learning session, review content, and learning record.

verification_guideline:
Sequencing and dependencies (follow roughly this order; most later checks depend on earlier data existing):
1) Sign in with the platform-provided identity first (learner A). Confirm the main workspace exposes the three areas and that switching between them works before creating any data.
2) Complete one full conversational intake as learner A using the fixed script: topic 'Basic conversational French', prior knowledge 'complete beginner', available time '2 hours before a dinner party this weekend', motivation 'to host a French-themed dinner party'. Answer one question per turn, wait for each AI turn to finish rendering before typing the next answer, and let the course generation complete before navigating away.
3) AI generation (intake→course path, session content, feedback, summaries, review plans) may take noticeably long. Always wait for streaming/loading indicators to settle; do not treat a still-loading pane as missing functionality, and do not re-submit the same input while a generation is in flight.
4) For the short-goal vs long-goal comparison and for the 'live AI' comparison, run additional intakes only after recording the first path (note its title, milestone count and milestone names first). Use: (a) same topic 'Basic conversational French' but time/motivation 'three months to reach mastery'; (b) a different topic 'Introductory linear algebra' with the same other answers. If the app supports multiple course paths, keep the original dinner-party path selectable and return to it for the session/vault checks; if the app only supports one active path, do these comparison runs LAST, after all Vault-related checks are done, since regenerating may reset course/progress state.
5) Before starting a session, record from Course Path: the ordered milestone/concept names, the marked next recommended concept, and the exact progress cue text (completed count, total, percentage). Re-read the same cue after finishing a session to compare.
6) For the Learning Session, open it from the Course Path start/continue control on the next recommended concept so the header concept can be matched. Within the session, work through the parts in the order the app presents them (explanation → recall question → quiz → practice task → example/diagram → finish/summary), submitting an answer for each interactive element and waiting for feedback before moving on.
7) Deliberate answer design: in the first session, answer the recall and quiz questions with clearly wrong answers on purpose (record how many questions there are and which ones you answered wrong) so that weak-area, review-plan and adaptive-review behaviour can later be observed. If a separate session is needed to check score arithmetic, answer all but exactly one question correctly and record the reported score against the total.
8) Complete the session fully (use the finish/complete/end-session control) — Vault updates, covered topics, summaries and progress increments typically only appear after the session is explicitly finished, not merely after answering questions.
9) Vault notes: save notes with unique, verbatim text so they cannot be confused with sample data — use exactly 'Remember bonjour vs bonsoir' for the note-saving check, and 'I already know greetings from a trip to Paris' for the continuity check. Save the continuity note BEFORE starting the follow-up session, then open a Learning Session for the next concept and read its introduction/review portion for explicit references to the stored note or the previously covered concept.
10) Persistence: only after the note is saved and at least one session is completed, reload the page as the same identity and reopen the Learning Vault to compare the same note text, covered topic and progress values. Reloading is for persistence only; do not use it as a substitute for observing in-app state updates.
11) Empty states: a Vault section (weak areas, review plans, prior summaries, saved materials) that is empty before any session is completed is an expected empty state, not a missing section — judge section presence from the Vault layout and judge population only after the relevant session is finished.
12) Identity isolation (multi-session): after learner A has a saved note and at least one covered topic, switch to a second, different platform identity (learner B) in a fresh session/profile. As learner B, open the Learning Vault directly and check whether learner A's unique note text and covered topics appear; do the check before creating any learner B data, then optionally create a distinct learner B note to confirm each vault shows only its own data. Return to learner A afterwards if further checks are needed.
13) Visual design and diagram checks are observational: capture full-view screenshots of intake, Course Path, Learning Session (including the diagram area) and Learning Vault, and judge the diagram's subject against the concept named in the session header.

title: Netlify People team internal tools
query: Build an internal Netlify People team portal for a remote HR team that wants to create and run its own People Ops software without engineers. The app should have a clean internal-tool interface with a left sidebar for Dashboard, Hiring Enablement, Employee Survey, Automations, and Build Studio. The Dashboard shows custom People analytics cards and charts, such as survey participation, open hiring enablement progress, and repeated workflow time saved, replacing a purchased analytics tool. The Hiring Enablement area is a self-service, gamified training path for new hiring managers: start with “Hiring Fundamentals,” embed Loom videos in each lesson, then ask interactive questions and short trivia quizzes about hiring principles, opening a role, and what structured hiring means. Show progress, completed modules, and quiz scores so People partners can use the manager’s self-study as preparation for a later live conversation. The Employee Survey tool lets the People team create surveys, collect employee responses, and view aggregated results in charts. Automations should turn manual People Operations steps into trackable workflows with triggers, owners, status, and weekly time-saved metrics. Build Studio should reflect the vibe-coding workflow: People team members describe a new internal tool in a prompt, use an AI/LLM assistant to generate or modify code, directly edit when needed, connect forms and analytics, then deploy the working tool to Netlify with one click. Use a lightweight, playful but professional style: clear cards, progress badges, quiz feedback, and concise helper copy for non-technical HR users.

- Quizzes: answer one question at a time and observe feedback immediately after each selection, before advancing. After finishing, navigate back to the Hiring Enablement overview (without retaking) to see whether module completion, progress and score are carried over; then check other, not-yet-completed modules on the same screen for comparison.
- Employee Survey: the app may start with no surveys of your own — an empty list plus a working create flow is not a missing feature. - Build Studio: submit the prompt 'Build a PTO request form with manager approval' and wait for generation to finish (allow for a loading/streaming state) before inspecting the code/preview. Then submit a clearly different prompt, 'Build an onboarding checklist tracker', in a fresh generation, and compare the two outputs for prompt-specific content; also observe whether a real backend/LLM request is issued (loading latency, streaming, network activity, or an error/api-key message) versus instant identical canned output. If an API key or model configuration is required, note the exact blocking message rather than retrying indefinitely.
- Build Studio follow-ups: after a successful generation, send the follow-up 'Add a comments field to the form' and check that the existing code/preview is modified rather than replaced by an unrelated template. Then click into the code editor so it has keyboard focus before typing a manual edit such as changing a heading to 'PTO Request v2', and check the preview afterwards (a manual re-run/preview refresh button, if present, is acceptable).
- Connections and deploy last: use the Build Studio controls to connect the generated tool to form handling and to analytics, observing the state indicator for each binding, then trigger the one-click deploy-to-Netlify action and wait for the progress state to resolve into a final result (URL, deployment id, or an explicit failure message) — record whatever final text/URL is shown.
- Dashboard re-check at the end: return to the Dashboard and read the survey participation and time-saved values again, comparing against your recorded baselines and the data you created. Use in-app navigation for this; a full page reload may be used only to check whether the created data persists, not as a substitute for observing in-app updates.

title: Paper Market
query: Build Paper Market, a dark financial-terminal web app where developers send automated agents into a simulated US stock market and humans only observe or connect agents. The landing dashboard should say “Only agents trade” and provide a clear “Connect agent” entry that registers an agent via API, grants exactly $1,000 paper cash, and lets it submit simulated trades using live US stock prices. Show top market stats such as Agents, Events, Volume, SPY, plus a market-status note like “US market closed — fills use last cached price.” The main layout should include a Stocks table with ticker, price, change, volume, and a tiny trend chart; an Agents leaderboard with tabs “Leaders / Losers / Bags / Rekt” ranked by net worth; and a read-only Agent chat area with ticker rooms like AMD, TSLA, META where agents post through the API. Implement real paper-trading account logic: orders update cash, holdings, net worth, total return, rank, and portfolio allocation without becoming real brokerage trading or investment advice. Add an agent profile page showing a PnL Snapshot, cash, holdings value, top holding, active status, portfolio list, a downloadable snapshot, and “Share on X.” Use a black grid background, card panels, monospaced numbers, green/red market coloring, ticker badges, and a slightly irreverent market-arena tone while keeping chat bounded by basic community moderation.

verification_guideline:
Order of work (many checkpoints depend on earlier steps succeeding):
1) Survey the landing dashboard read-only first (top stats block, tagline, market-status note, Stocks table, leaderboard tabs, chat rooms, disclaimer copy, background/typography/badges). Record verbatim any numbers or notes you will need later before creating data.
2) Then use the "Connect agent" entry to register a new agent, then place trades for it, then inspect its profile, then re-check the leaderboard/rank, then reload for persistence. Do not attempt trade/PnL/allocation/rank/profile checkpoints before a fresh agent exists.

Agent registration and API usage:
- Open the "Connect agent" entry and read the on-screen registration/API documentation carefully (endpoint paths, key/token issuance, required headers and body fields, and how orders and chat posts are submitted). Follow exactly the paths the app itself documents; do not invent endpoints or assume a REST convention.
- Register the agent under the name "TestBot" plus a short unique marker (e.g. TestBot_7421) so it can never be confused with seeded demo agents. Save the issued key/token in the very first response — some apps show it only once.
- If the app also offers a UI shortcut that performs the same registration, prefer the documented API path; only fall back to the UI button if no API call is possible from the browser environment. In-page tools such as a built-in console/playground, or issuing fetch calls from the browser address/dev context, are acceptable execution routes as long as the documented endpoint and credential are used.
- Immediately after registration and before any trade, open the new agent's account/profile view and record its cash, net worth, and holdings state.

Trading sequence (keep it minimal and deterministic):
- Before ordering, read and write down the AMD price shown in the Stocks table (and the SPY stat, plus one other ticker such as TSLA).
- Submit a buy of 1 share of AMD first (confirms the order path is accepted and the position surfaces), then a second buy so the agent ends with 2 AMD shares total — or submit a single 2-share order if you prefer, but then verify the 1-share acceptance step differently. Record the fill price returned/displayed.
- To exercise the "top holding" logic, add a second, clearly smaller-value position in a different ticker with the remaining cash so the profile has at least two positions.
- After trading, re-read cash, holdings value, net worth, total return, allocation percentages and rank from the agent's account/profile view and compute the relationships yourself from the displayed numbers.

Real-market data authenticity (mandatory, do not judge from the page alone):
- After recording the on-page prices for AMD, TSLA and SPY (and the recorded fill price), consult an external ground-truth source (e.g. a public finance site or search result for the same tickers) in a separate tab, note whether the US session is open or closed at the moment of testing, and compare the page values against the live price or last close. Report both the page value and the external value.

Chat checkpoints:
- Inspect the chat panel as a human first: confirm which ticker rooms exist and whether any composer/send control is available or explicitly restricted; switch from the AMD room to the TSLA room and observe whether the active room and message list change (this is a UI state change, not real-time sync — no reload needed).
- Then post via the registered agent's credentials through the documented chat API: first the exact message "ping-from-agent" to the AMD room, and observe the AMD room without reloading to see whether it appears attributed to the agent. Only if it does not appear within a reasonable wait may you reload once and note that fact.
- For moderation, post a second message from the same agent containing clearly abusive/profane wording, and record the API response and exactly how (or whether) it renders in the room.

Profile page, snapshot and share:
- Reach the profile by clicking the agent's entry in the leaderboard (this also covers the navigation relationship); confirm the identity shown matches the marked test agent name.
- Trigger the snapshot download control and record what artifact is produced (file name/type or generated image/JSON), and trigger "Share on X" and record the target URL/prefilled text without needing to complete any external login.

Persistence and empty-state cautions:
- Only for persistence: reload the page and reopen the same agent's account view to compare cash, AMD position and net worth against the pre-reload values.
- If a leaderboard tab, chat room, or portfolio list appears empty, distinguish a legitimate empty state (no qualifying agents/messages yet) from a broken feature; where feasible, create the minimal data needed (e.g. an agent whose net worth drops) before concluding.
- Note any hard rate limits, cooldowns, or market-closed order rejections stated by the app; if the app enforces a wait before an action becomes available, advance time only after that timer has actually started.

title: The Ultimate Life Management System
query:
I want to build “The Ultimate Life Management System”, a clean Notion-style personal life management app for people tired of juggling notes, goals, habits, finances, and daily tasks across separate tools. Use a light, minimal table-database layout on mobile or narrow screens, with a home sidebar or top section linking key areas like Personal, Financial, Health, and Business. The main modules should include Goals Hub, Finance Center, Habit Tracker, plus simple Notes and Daily Tasks sections. In Goals Hub, show a database table with view switching such as “All Goals”, search, filter and sort controls, a blue add button, and editable fields for Goal, Category, Priority, and Deadline; include an example like “Run a 5K / Health / Medium / September 1, 2026”. Finance Center should follow the flow “Transactions → Budget → Debt & Loan Planning → Goals → Monthly snapshot” and let users record transaction name, type, amount, and category, with an example Paycheck income of $2,200. Habit Tracker should track Habit, Area, Frequency, and Streak in days, including a daily health habit like “Drink 2L water”. Every table should support adding a “New page” row, editing records, searching, filtering, sorting, and switching between overview and active-style views. Add a persistent bottom “Ask AI” input that can answer questions and assist with the user’s stored goals, finances, habits, notes, and tasks, such as summarizing what needs attention this week. Keep the visual tone calm and productivity-focused: white background, large page titles, subtle dividers, rounded table cells, pastel tags like Health, Medium, Income, and Daily, and one clear blue primary add action.

Within Finance Center, add a Debt & Loan Planning area for private personal estimates. A Debt Time view lets the user enter total debt balance, effective hourly take-home pay, and normal work hours per day; it immediately converts the balance into required work hours and work days, shows the underlying formula, provides an empty state, and keeps the data private to the host identity. A Loan Planner lets the user enter loan amount, annual interest rate, and tenure in years, then calculates monthly EMI, total interest, and total repayment using the standard reducing-balance formula. It should show a year-by-year amortization table with opening balance, principal paid, interest paid, total payment, and closing balance. Users may save and compare private loan scenarios. Any optional rate preset is creator-maintained, manually adjustable, and visibly labeled as an example rather than live lender data. Show a concise note that actual rates, fees, eligibility, and lender approval can differ.

verification_guideline:
Operate in a fixed order so later checks build on earlier ones, and reset any filter/search/sort state before starting the next check.

1. Start from the home/landing view and first inventory the navigation shell (area links such as Personal, Financial, Health, Business and the module entry points) before opening anything. 2. Note where the app renders on a narrow/mobile-style layout: if the sidebar collapses into a menu or top section, open that menu first rather than concluding the links are absent.
3. Goals Hub order: (a) read the pre-seeded rows and their column fields; (b) add a new row via the primary add action / 'New page' row and commit the name before touching other cells; (c) edit an existing row's Priority; (d) test search; (e) clear search, then test filter; (f) clear filter, then test sort; (g) finally switch views. Always clear the previous control before applying the next one, otherwise combined state will make later results ambiguous.
4. Use unique, identifiable test content for every record you create (e.g. append a short marker or timestamp such as 'Read 12 Books T27' where the checkpoint's exact text is not required, and keep the exact required text where it is). This prevents confusing seeded sample data with your own additions.
5. After any inline edit (cell, dropdown, date field), commit it explicitly (press Enter, blur the field, or close the editor popup) and re-read the row from the table view rather than from the open editor.
6. Finance Center order: first scroll the whole page top-to-bottom once to record the sequence of the flow sections before interacting; then add a transaction in the Transactions area; then open the Debt & Loan Planning area. Data created in Transactions may be expected to affect other sections (e.g. snapshot/goals) — check those after the record is committed, not before.
7. Debt Time: check the blank/cleared state first (before typing anything) so the empty state can be observed, then type the values into the three inputs one field at a time and observe whether results update without any page reload or explicit submit. Read the displayed hours/days values and the displayed formula text verbatim.
8. Loan Planner: enter amount, rate and tenure, trigger the calculation if a calculate action exists, and record the exact EMI / total interest / total repayment figures and the amortization rows as displayed (do not round in your notes). Then save the current result as a named scenario with a unique name, change the inputs to a clearly different loan, calculate and save a second uniquely named scenario, and only after two scenarios exist open the comparison view. If a rate preset control exists, apply it, then manually edit the rate field afterwards to confirm it is still editable, and record any label/disclaimer wording near it verbatim.
9. Multi-session (privacy of Debt & Loan Planning): use exactly two identities. As the host identity, first complete the Debt Time entry and save at least one uniquely named loan scenario, and note the exact figures/scenario name. Then switch to a second, separate identity (platform identity switch / separate session, not just a new tab of the same identity) and open Finance Center → Debt & Loan Planning there, checking whether the host's figures, results, or the uniquely named scenario appear. Do not modify data from the second identity before this observation. Afterwards return to the host identity to confirm its own data is still intact.
10. Habit Tracker: verify the column set first, then add a habit row, edit its Frequency, then exercise search / filter / sort / view switching one at a time with a reset in between, and finally locate the seeded daily health habit row and read its Area, Frequency and Streak cells.
11. Notes and Daily Tasks: create the item, then re-open or navigate away and back to the section to confirm the created item and its state (e.g. completion) are still shown. Empty lists on first entry are a legitimate starting state, not evidence of missing functionality — create data before judging.
12. Ask AI: after visiting each of the five modules, check whether the input stays anchored at the bottom in each of them (scroll to the bottom of long pages, since a long table can push the page content). Send one question that references data you actually created (using your unique marker) and record the full response text; allow a reasonable wait for a streamed answer before concluding.
13. Persistence checks (reload/re-entry) are only appropriate for confirming that stored records survive; do not use a reload as a substitute for observing whether an input recomputes immediately.

title: HOOD RUN
query: Build a retro pixel-art web game called HOOD RUN, a lightweight dodge-and-run arcade game for the $HOODIE community, playable on both mobile and desktop browsers. Open on a classic bordered pop-up main menu styled like an 8-bit dialog: show the big title HOOD RUN, the subtitle 'dodge the bears & FUD', a HI-SCORE line displaying the current best score, a quick legend ('POLES = AVOID' and '1 COIN = +5 PTS'), and a chunky pixel 'RUN IT' button to start. The whole thing sits on a dark brown-amber night cityscape with a pixel skyline, moon, drifting clouds and twinkling stars. Tapping RUN IT drops you into the game, where you steer a small pixel flying character (the community mascot) through a side-scrolling stage: it keeps moving forward while you dodge oncoming poles and bears/FUD obstacles, and grab floating coins that add 5 points each. Support both touch controls on mobile and keyboard (tap/space to fly up or hop) on PC, with tight collision detection, a live score counter climbing during play, and a game-over state on collision that shows your final score and updates the persisted HI-SCORE if you beat it, then lets you retry back to the menu. Add snappy pixel animations for the character, coins and obstacles, plus subtle retro sound cues. Keep the difficulty rising gently as the run gets longer. Treat the $HOODIE community branding and any contract-address text purely as decorative retro theming in the footer, not as a functional or financial feature. Overall vibe: crunchy 8-bit visuals, fast fun loop, instant to pick up.

verification_guideline:
Order of operations (each later step depends on the earlier one succeeding):
1. Load the app at a desktop viewport (e.g. 1280×800) and first inspect the opening menu dialog as a whole (title, subtitle, HI-SCORE line, legend lines, start button) and the backdrop, plus the footer branding area — scroll the page if the footer is below the fold. Record the HI-SCORE value shown at this moment; you will need it later.
2. Before starting a run, stay on the menu for ~3-5 seconds and take at least two screenshots several seconds apart (do not move the mouse or press keys in between) so that any background motion (clouds/stars) can be compared frame-to-frame rather than judged from a single still.
3. Start a run via the start control. Immediately after the stage appears, take a screenshot and note the initial score value.

Gameplay observation:
- For automatic forward motion, deliberately give NO input for ~3 seconds and compare consecutive screenshots for horizontal movement of background/obstacles; do not confuse the player's own falling with stage scrolling.
- For keyboard control, click once on the game stage/canvas area first so it holds focus, then press the fly key and capture screenshots immediately before and immediately after the press to compare the character's vertical position. Take the 'after' screenshot fast (within a few hundred ms) because gravity pulls the character back down.
- For sprite animation, take screenshots at short intervals (~300 ms) while the run is active and compare character/coin/obstacle poses; do not rely on a single screenshot.
- Coin scoring: read the score immediately before steering into a coin and immediately after pickup; verify the delta, and avoid frames where the passive score tick could confound the reading (compare the increment against the normal per-frame drift you observed).
- Collision: to reach a game-over deliberately, stop giving input (or fly into an obstacle) so the run ends; capture the live score in the last frame before the game-over overlay so it can be compared with the final score shown.
- If the run is very long, do not busy-wait with dozens of screenshots; use time advancement only for genuinely long waits, and note that a running game loop may be driven by animation frames, so prefer real observation over time skipping for gameplay motion.

Difficulty progression:
- Survive one long run (aim for ~45-60 s of play) by using the fly control repeatedly, and capture comparable screenshot pairs early (first ~10 s) and late in the run; judge speed by the displacement of the same kind of object between two screenshots taken with the same interval, and/or by how many obstacles are on screen at once.

Hi-score sequence (must be done in this exact order):
- First run: try to score as high as reasonably possible, then note the final score on the game-over screen, return to the menu via the retry/back control, and read the menu HI-SCORE.
- Second run: intentionally end the run very quickly (e.g. crash almost immediately) so the final score is clearly lower, return to the menu and read the HI-SCORE again.
- Only after these two runs, reload the page and read the menu HI-SCORE once more for the persistence check. Reloading may only be used for persistence, not as a substitute for observing live in-game updates.

Mobile pass:
- Switch to a 375×812 viewport with touch emulation and reload. Re-check that the menu dialog and, after starting, the running stage fit without horizontal overflow or clipped title/score/controls, and perform a tap on the game area during a run, comparing character position immediately before and after the tap.

Sound cues:
- Audio cannot be heard; check for evidence of a retro sound cue at the moment of a coin pickup or a collision (e.g. an audio element or a Web Audio context becoming active/ resuming). Note that browsers may keep audio suspended until the first user gesture, so ensure a click/keypress has already occurred before judging.

General:
- Distinguish an empty/initial state (e.g. HI-SCORE showing 0 on a fresh profile) from a missing feature; a zero starting hi-score is a legitimate initial state.
- Treat footer branding/contract text as decorative: only confirm it is static text without transactional controls; do not attempt any financial interaction.
- If a run ends unexpectedly during any measurement, restart from the menu and repeat that measurement rather than inferring results from partial data.

title: Widelands
query: Build a playable Web App version of Widelands, an open-source real-time strategy game inspired by Settlers II, focused on island building and resource economy. Use a top-down isometric map with a retro 2D hand-drawn look: forests, water, sandy beaches, rocky hills, and buildings connected by roads, plus harbor, boats, and lighthouse details for a coastal settlement feel. The core loop is a single-player playable slice on one small scenario map: players place buildings (like woodcutter's hut, quarry, warehouse, and a headquarters) onto grid tiles, watch workers gather raw materials such as wood, stone, and food, then route those resources along roads to where they're needed to expand the settlement. Give each building a placement preview, a cost check against current resources, and a small info panel showing what it produces or consumes; keep live resource counters at the top that update in real time as production ticks. Let players scroll and zoom the map to explore terrain and decide where to grow. Instead of real online multiplayer, offer a skirmish mode against a simple AI opponent on the same map, where the AI also builds and competes for territory, so the strategy tension stays without needing a live server. Add a single-player scenario with a clear goal (for example, reach a target amount of a key resource or claim a landmark) and a simple win/complete state. Keep the interface cozy and game-like with wooden UI panels and an isometric camera, and manage all building, worker, and resource state on the front end so the whole match runs smoothly in the browser.

verification_guideline:
Suggested order of verification (later steps depend on earlier ones succeeding):
1) Entry screen first: record what modes are offered before clicking anything. Start the single-player scenario mode first and complete all scenario-related checks (map, HUD, build menu, placement, roads, production, objective) before switching to skirmish, since re-entering a mode usually resets the match state.
2) Immediately after the map loads, take stock of the starting state: the initial values of every resource counter in the top bar, any pre-placed starting buildings (headquarters/warehouse), and the stated objective text with its target. Record these numbers verbatim — later cost-deduction and production checks compare against them.
3) Camera checks (pan and zoom) should be done early, before placing buildings, so the map surface is unchanged. Try more than one interaction channel for each: drag on the map body, arrow/edge keys, and any on-screen pan/zoom controls plus the mouse wheel over the map area. Click once on the map canvas first so it holds keyboard focus before pressing keys. Judge pan/zoom by comparing the visible terrain/tile size between two screenshots, not by the presence of a control.
4) Terrain and coastal details: use panning/zooming to survey the whole map before building. Note where forest, water, beach, and rocky/hill tiles are, and look along the coastline for harbor/boat/lighthouse objects. Zoom in enough to judge sprite style rather than judging from a shrunken view.
5) Building placement sequence: open the build menu and record every offered building type together with its listed cost and any produces/consumes description shown on hover/selection. Then select the woodcutter's hut, hover over at least two different tiles to observe whether the preview follows the cursor, and only then click a valid empty land tile adjacent to forest. Immediately re-read the resource counters and compare with the pre-placement values you recorded and with the listed cost. Place the quarry adjacent to rocky/hill tiles the same way.
6) Cost check: to test unaffordable placement, pick the most expensive building in the menu (or spend down resources first by placing cheap buildings) and attempt placement; record whether the entry is disabled, the preview turns invalid, a message appears, and whether the building appears on the map and whether counters change.
7) Roads and routing: after production buildings exist, activate the road tool explicitly, then click a connecting sequence of tiles from the production building toward the headquarters/warehouse and confirm/finish the path as the UI requires. Keep at least one producing building deliberately unconnected if possible so the connected vs. unconnected difference can be observed.
8) Production and timing: production and AI expansion are tick-based. Start the wait only after the buildings/roads exist, then use advance_time (or wait) in one or two chunks of roughly 30–60 seconds rather than many tiny steps, and do not click, spend resources, or reload the page during the wait window. Re-read the same counters and the goal progress indicator after each wait, and compare with the values recorded before the wait. Do not refresh the page to observe production — production is real-time state, and reloading may reset the match.
9) Workers: while waiting, take two or more screenshots a few seconds apart of the same map region around a production building at a zoom level where sprites are distinguishable, to judge whether worker figures actually move.
10) Win state: check whether the objective can plausibly be reached by letting production run with advance_time; if the target is large, build several producing buildings connected by roads first and then advance time repeatedly, checking after each advance. If any developer/debug or speed control exists, it may be used, but record that it was used. If the objective is a landmark rather than a resource total, drive toward that condition instead.
11) Skirmish mode: return to the entry screen (main menu entry, or reload if no menu path exists) and start skirmish. Record how the AI opponent is identified (label, legend, color, or its settlement), capture a screenshot of the map immediately at match start, then wait ~60 seconds without any player action and compare building counts/positions on the AI side against the initial screenshot. Also note whether player-owned and AI-owned buildings/territory use different colors or markers.
12) UI style checks (wooden panels, hand-drawn art) should be judged from full-view screenshots of the HUD, build menu, and info panel; state what is actually rendered rather than the code intent.
13) Empty or minimal starting state (e.g., no roads, no player buildings, zero of some resource) at match start is expected, not evidence of missing functionality; only judge a feature missing after attempting the corresponding interaction.

title: Content Brief Agent
query:
Build a mobile-friendly web app that helps content marketers, SEO specialists, and bloggers turn a single keyword into a ready-to-use content brief in seconds. The core experience is one clean input screen: a field for the target keyword plus an optional "site context" box where the user pastes a short note about their site or existing content clusters (used to inform internal linking suggestions). A prominent "Generate Brief" button kicks off the platform AI, which produces a structured, publication-ready brief rather than generic filler. The generated brief should be laid out in clearly separated sections on a results page: the target keyword with about five semantic variations, the inferred search intent, three suggested title options, a full H2/H3 outline, a recommended word-count target, a set of "People Also Ask" style questions, internal linking suggestions grounded in the pasted site context, and a competitor-gap paragraph highlighting angles worth covering. Since the brief is built from AI analysis of the keyword and any details the user provides, let users optionally paste in a few competitor page notes or SERP snippets to sharpen the competitive analysis; the AI folds these into its intent and gap sections. Each section should be a rounded card with a copy button, plus a "copy full brief" and download-as-text action so the user can move it into their own doc and spend their remaining time fine-tuning the outline. Keep the interface light and focused—an efficient single-flow tool with a subtle loading state showing the brief is being assembled, and a clean, readable typographic layout suited to reviewing long-form outlines on both desktop and mobile.

Add a second, clearly labeled Existing Copy mode for marketers who already have writing to improve. In this mode, the user pastes text, selects Type (email, blog, social caption, essay, or general), Tone (neutral, professional, casual, or friendly), and Length (keep same length, shorter, or slightly expanded). The user can choose Correct Grammar for grammar, punctuation, spelling, and sentence-mechanics corrections only, or Refine for a more polished rewrite guided by the selected controls. Show the result in a separate editable output card, label it Grammar-only or Refined, and provide clear/reset and copy actions. This mode should remain separate from the keyword-to-brief flow and use the same focused, mobile-friendly writing-tool interface.

verification_guideline:
Suggested execution order (each phase depends on the previous one succeeding):
1. Landing survey: on first load, note the mode control set (tabs/segmented control) and confirm which mode is active by default. Do not switch modes yet.
2. Keyword brief input: in the keyword mode, fill all three inputs in one pass before generating — target keyword 'cold brew coffee', site context 'Our blog already has clusters on espresso machines and burr grinders', and competitor/SERP notes 'Competitor pages only cover brewing ratios and never discuss caffeine content or cost per cup'. Take a screenshot showing the entered values still visible in their fields before clicking Generate.
3. Loading state: click 'Generate Brief' and immediately capture a screenshot (without waiting) so any transient assembling/loading indicator is recorded; then wait for generation to finish (AI calls may take 15–60s) and capture the completed results view. If nothing appears after a long wait, retry the generation once before concluding.
4. Read the results in one continuous scroll pass, capturing every section card (keyword + variations, intent, titles, outline, word count, PAA, internal links, competitor gap). Record the actual on-screen text of the variations, titles, internal-link items and gap paragraph verbatim in your notes — later comparisons depend on this transcript.
5. Clipboard checks: for copy actions, always paste into a real editable text field to inspect what was actually copied. Use an empty text area in the app itself (e.g. the Existing Copy source box or the site-context box, cleared afterwards) or the browser address bar, and clear it after reading. Do a per-section copy (e.g. the outline card) first, verify its scope, then the 'copy full brief' action, so the clipboard contents of the two are not confused.
6. Download: trigger the download-as-text action, then open/inspect the downloaded file's contents rather than judging from the toast alone.
7. Regeneration comparison: return to the keyword input (via the app's own back/new-brief affordance or the mode control) and generate a second brief for 'commercial roof inspection' with the same or empty context fields. Compare its variations/titles/outline/gap text against the transcript from step 4 rather than relying on memory.
8. Mobile layout: only after the desktop pass, resize the viewport to 390x844 with a brief already displayed, then scroll the full brief top-to-bottom checking for horizontal overflow, clipping, or overlap. Restore the desktop viewport before continuing.
9. Existing Copy mode: switch via the mode control, then (a) enumerate all options in Type, Tone and Length controls by opening each control; (b) paste 'we was planning to launch the produkt next week, its going to be greatt.' and run 'Correct Grammar', recording the output text and its label; (c) clear or replace with a 2–3 sentence paragraph of your own (include a short unique marker word so you can tell outputs apart), and run 'Refine' with Type=blog, Tone=professional, Length=keep same length.
10. Control-influence checks: keep the exact same source paragraph across runs; change only Tone (casual vs professional) and re-run Refine, then change only Length (shorter vs slightly expanded) and re-run. Capture each output separately and note approximate word counts so the comparisons are made on identical input.
11. Editability, clear and copy in Existing Copy mode: after a Refine output exists, click into the output card and type a distinctive marker string to test editing; then test the copy action (paste elsewhere to confirm) and finally the clear/reset action, checking both input and output areas. Perform clear last, since it destroys the state needed by the other checks.
12. Mode separation: after using Existing Copy mode, switch back to the keyword-brief mode and confirm what is and isn't displayed there; note whether previously entered keyword-mode state persists — an emptied form or a fresh input screen is a legitimate design and is not itself a missing feature.
General stability notes: AI-generated text differs run to run, so never re-run a generation when the current output already answers the question; always transcribe on-screen text before navigating away. If a generation fails with an error, retry once and record the error text if it persists.

title: Drone Warfare
query: Build a Web App game prototype called Drone Warfare: a browser-based FPV combat simulator where the player pilots a small attack drone in manual acro flight over a large, low-contrast battlefield. The experience should feel like a live military drone feed, with a dark green night-vision HUD, thin tactical frames, a central aiming reticle, and real-time telemetry such as LQ, RSSI, LAT, ALT, SPD, BAT, throttle/yaw, and pitch/roll. The main screen is the cockpit view: keyboard or pointer controls change throttle, yaw, pitch, and roll, immediately updating drone attitude, speed, altitude, camera tilt, and HUD readouts. Add a mission layer with a prompt like “ARMOR HUNT: BREAK THE HOSTILE MECHANIZED LINE,” objective progress such as 0/3, score, kills, misses, base integrity, wave number, and launch status. Populate the battlefield with moving armor and infantry targets that can be tracked, attacked, damaged, and counted toward the objective. Include enemy jammers and a Pantsir-style sector air defense system that scans for the drone, creates radar contacts, launches interceptors, and forces the player to stay low, use terrain, and outfly incoming missiles. Add a right-side tactical panel for “SECTOR AIR DEFENSE,” “RADAR / INTERCEPT CONTROL,” selected track status, contacts, and interceptors, plus visible warning states when radar sweep or missile lock is active. Weapon hits, crashes, missed shots, target kills, objective completion, and drone loss should update the combat statistics in real time. Keep the app focused on a playable single-session simulation with restart/launch controls and a platform preview/share entry for access, using local simulated battlefield logic rather than external deployment or live services. The visual tone should be tense, minimal, and tactical: monochrome green UI, scanline-like overlays, subtle HUD flicker, and sparse mission copy such as “Keep low. Read the treeline. Commit only with a clean link.”
